verses.text: Josiah celebrated the Passover for the LORD in Jerusalem. They killed the Passover lambs on the fourteenth day of the first month.
He gave the priests their duties and encouraged them in their work in the LORD's temple.

He said to the Levites, who taught all Israel and had been set apart for the LORD, "Put the holy ark in the temple that Solomon son of David, king of Israel, built. You do not need to carry it on your shoulders any more. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel.
Get ready by your families and groups, as David king of Israel and his son Solomon wrote down.
Stand in the holy place with a group of Levites for each family group of your relatives, the ordinary people.
Kill the Passover lambs, make yourselves holy, and prepare the lambs for your relatives, doing what the LORD commanded through Moses."

Josiah gave the people thirty thousand lambs and young goats from his own flocks for the Passover offerings, for everyone who was there. He also gave three thousand bulls. All these came from the king's own property.

His officials also gave freely to the people, the priests, and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the officials in charge of God's temple, gave the priests two thousand six hundred lambs and goats and three hundred cattle for the Passover offerings.

Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the leaders of the Levites, gave the Levites five thousand lambs and goats and five hundred cattle for the Passover offerings.
When everything was ready for the service, the priests stood in their places, and the Levites in their groups, as the king had ordered.
They killed the Passover lambs. The priests sprinkled the blood the Levites handed them, and the Levites skinned the animals.
They set aside the parts for burnt offerings to give to the people by their family groups, to offer to the LORD as written in the book of Moses. They did the same with the cattle.
They roasted the Passover lambs over the fire, as the law says. They boiled the holy offerings in pots, kettles, and pans, and quickly served them to all the people.

After that, the Levites prepared food for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the descendants of Aaron, were busy offering the burnt offerings and the fat until night. So the Levites prepared food for themselves and for the priests.

The singers, the descendants of Asaph, were in their places, as David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's seer had ordered. The gatekeepers stood at each gate. They did not need to leave their posts, because their relatives the Levites prepared food for them.
So on that day the whole service of the LORD was carried out, to celebrate the Passover and to offer burnt offerings on the LORD's altar, as King Josiah had ordered.
The Israelites who were there celebrated the Passover at that time, and the Festival of Bread Without Yeast for seven days.

No Passover like this had been celebrated in Israel since the days of the prophet Samuel. None of the kings of Israel had ever celebrated a Passover like the one Josiah celebrated, with the priests, the Levites, all the people of Judah and Israel who were there, and the people of Jerusalem.
This Passover was celebrated in the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule.
After all this, when Josiah had set the temple in order, Neco king of Egypt went to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates River. Josiah went out to fight against him.

But Neco sent messengers to him, saying, "What do you have against me, king of Judah? I am not coming to attack you today, but the kingdom I am at war with. God has told me to hurry. Stop fighting against God, who is with me, or he will destroy you."
But Josiah would not turn back. He disguised himself to fight him. He did not listen to what Neco said, though the message came from God. He went to fight in the plain of Megiddo.
Archers shot King Josiah, and he told his officers, "Take me away. I am badly wounded!"

So his officers took him out of his chariot, put him in his other chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem. There he died and was buried in the tombs of his ancestors. All the people of Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.

Jeremiah wrote sad songs about Josiah. To this day, all the men and women singers still remember Josiah in their sad songs. These songs became a custom in Israel, and they are written in the book of Laments.
Everything else Josiah did, and his faithful acts in obeying what is written in the LORD's law,
all his acts from beginning to end, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
